headline: North American copper scrap drops 25 cents a pound in one day
detail: On Nov 24 the main clean copper grades fell 25 cents/lb, erasing the prior day's gain, while brass slipped up to 8 cents and many aluminum grades 1-4 cents; ferrous and stainless held flat. Yard copper and brass bids are swinging hard with the futures selloff.

headline: LME copper drops to an 11-month low as rate-hike fears hit metals
detail: Three-month LME copper fell about 1.9% to roughly $11,596/t on Wednesday, down about 18% this month, as funds sold on hot inflation, a firm dollar and AI-spending doubts; tin fell 7% and zinc hit a 6-month low. Expect softer bids on copper and brass scrap.

headline: Core PCE inflation runs hot and Q3 GDP is revised up, locking in a December Fed hike
detail: October core PCE came in at 3.3% and Q3 growth was revised to 4.3%, pushing odds of a quarter-point hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting above 90%. Higher rates and a firm dollar weigh on base metals and credit-funded steel demand.

headline: Scrap expected to keep rising after lagging the steel rally
detail: Steel Market Update notes hot-rolled coil climbed sharply this year while busheling lagged, and scrap is now expected to firm on seasonal factors and tight supply. That points to a steady-to-higher December settle for prime and obsolete grades.

headline: Platinum and palladium bounce late Wednesday after a rough week
detail: Kitco quotes show platinum near $1,303 and palladium near $864 early Thursday, up about 2% after both hit multi-month lows last week. Converter values remain well below a year ago, with palladium about a third lower.

headline: Copper bounces back above $5.40 on Thursday
detail: COMEX copper climbed about 1.5% to around $5.41/lb as tech stocks recovered and the new tariff proposals looked less disruptive than feared. The bounce follows an 11-month low, so scrap bids may steady.

headline: Aluminum falls to a 13-month low as the LME tightens lending rules
detail: London aluminum slid to about $2,745/t after the LME cut its lending threshold to 30% from 50%, which collapsed the cash premium over three-month metal, and China's output heads for a record. Lower primary prices weigh on aluminum scrap values.

headline: US proposes new tariffs of up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 other countries
detail: The proposed Section 301 duties target overcapacity, with 20% for China and Vietnam and up to 15% for the EU, Japan and Korea; hearings come first, so they likely won't start before next year. Steel and aluminum are left out because Section 232 already covers them, but the escalation hit risk appetite.

headline: Chinese steel output falls again as only about 10% of mills make money
detail: October crude steel output fell 6.9% from September to about 70.8 Mt and hot-metal output has dropped six weeks running on weak construction. Weaker Chinese steel demand caps global steel and ferrous scrap prices and may push out more cheap exports.

headline: Cox expects November new-vehicle sales at a 15.8 million annual pace
detail: Volume should be about 1.2 million units, down from a year ago on fewer selling days, but the pace is up from October. Steady sales keep stamping plants running and prime busheling flowing.

headline: US copper premium turns to a discount and stockpiled metal heads back to China
detail: With LME copper about 20% below its September peak, the US price is now below London, so tariff-driven US stocks are being shipped out, mostly to China, where import premiums hit a record. That is bearish for domestic copper scrap spreads.

headline: Nucor raises its hot-rolled coil price again, to $1,330 a ton
detail: Nucor lifted its weekly HRC spot price by $20 with lead times of three to five weeks, and buyers don't expect a drop soon. Strong sheet prices keep mills hungry for prime scrap and support busheling bids.

headline: US scrap export market stays quiet as Turkish buying slows
detail: The last confirmed US cargo to Turkey was in late October near $398.50/t CFR for HMS 80:20, and Turkish mills have since bought sparingly from Europe. Weak export demand removes a prop for obsolete grades.

headline: Palladium slid to about $872 last week, cutting catalytic converter values
detail: Palladium dropped about 5% on Nov 20 on weak auto demand and rate-hike worries. Lower palladium means refiners pay less for gasoline-engine converters.

headline: Dollar holds near 103.75 as Treasury yields slip to a 3-month low
detail: The dollar is off its recent 20-month high while the 10-year yield fell to about 4.80% on haven buying. A strong dollar still keeps pressure on dollar-priced metals.

headline: Chinese copper scrap prices fall sharply
detail: On Nov 25 Chinese bare bright and #1/#2 copper scrap each fell 4,500 yuan/t, with brass and aluminum grades lower too. Weaker Chinese scrap buying can hold down export bids for US nonferrous scrap.

headline: Vanke seeks a three-year delay on a bond payment as property stress deepens
detail: The developer wants to push back a 1.2 billion yuan payment due Dec 15, with its sales down nearly half. More property distress means less construction steel demand in the biggest metals market.

headline: October new home sales jump 14% to the best pace of 2026
detail: Sales rose to a 701,000 annual pace as builders cut prices, though the Midwest is still down for the year. A modest lift for rebar, wire and HVAC copper demand.

headline: Fed Beige Book says construction weakened while manufacturing grew modestly
detail: Most districts saw slight growth, but residential real estate and construction softened on high borrowing costs, and contacts named metals and tariffs as cost pressures. Mixed signal for steel and scrap demand.

headline: Durable goods orders edge up, with primary metals shipments rising 1.5%
detail: October orders rose 0.2% and core capital goods orders 1.2%, with primary metals the biggest contributor to the shipments gain. Firm factory investment supports industrial scrap generation and mill demand.

headline: Jobless claims fall to 189,000, matching the year's low
detail: Claims dropped 13,000, well below forecasts. A tight job market strengthens the case for a Fed hike, a headwind for metal prices.

headline: Gold briefly breaks below $3,500 after hot inflation data, then recovers
detail: Gold dipped to about $3,476/oz and silver near $39.37 after the PCE report, before both rebounded late in the day to around $3,588 and $41.28 on Kitco. Rate-hike odds and the dollar keep precious metals volatile.

headline: First Quantum accepts Panama's terms for talks on Cobre Panama
detail: Formal talks on the mine, shut since 2023 and once about 1% of world copper supply, began Nov 23. A restart is still far off but raises the prospect of more copper later.

headline: Chinese zinc smelters restart after maintenance
detail: Smelters in several provinces came back online, adding refined supply and pushing zinc lower even as mine supply stays tight. Adds pressure on zinc and die-cast scrap values.

headline: Silver rebounds toward $41.50 early Thursday
detail: Kitco shows silver up about 0.6% and gold down about 0.4% in thin holiday trading after Wednesday's swings. Low Thanksgiving liquidity can exaggerate moves.

headline: Iron ore stays near a four-year low
detail: Chinese iron ore futures hit a four-year low in mid-November and 62% Fe sat near $89-91/t on weak steel output and high port stocks. Cheap ore helps blast furnaces compete with scrap-fed mills overseas.

headline: Stellantis sues Unifor over the idled Brampton plant as talks continue
detail: Stellantis says the union blocked access needed to sell the plant to a defence firm; about 2,200 workers remain laid off. Detroit Three production in Canada keeps shrinking.

headline: Nickel slips to a five-week low
detail: Nickel fell to about $15,164/t on Nov 24 as the market stays in surplus. That keeps pressure on stainless and nickel-alloy scrap.

headline: EV sales pick up but dealers are short on inventory after production cuts
detail: October EV sales rose about 11% from a year ago, helped by higher gas prices, but dealer EV stock is down 38% after GM and Ford cut output. Low EV output limits aluminum and copper demand in vehicles.

headline: Platinum council sees the market swinging to a deficit in 2027
detail: WPIC forecasts a 279,000 oz shortfall next year after a surplus in 2026, on weaker South African supply. That gives some medium-term support to converter values.
